Why do acids seem to be so much more common in nature, and in particular foods, than bases?
Because glucose is needed for cellular respiration and glucose is an acid.
There's nothing basic that's required on a cellular or macro level?

Not exactly. Off of the top of my head, your blood is a buffer solution. Buffer solutions mitigate large changes in pH because they have specific proportions of an acid/base and its conjugate. This is necessary because, were your blood to become more acidic, you would experience acidosis. (There's a similar condition for high basicity, but I can't remember what it is.)

It is interesting, though, that I can't think of a ton of bases that are common in carbon-based life. Though this may be just a lack of knowledge on my part. I think the glucose explanation is a very good one.

Not in the same way. Glucose breaks down to form ATP. ATP powers your cell. Without ATP you die super fast. Crazy fast. To make sure you never run out of ATP your body keeps a large amount of glucose on hand. This happens in plants and animals. This increases acidity by virtue of there just being a fuck ton of glucose hanging about.
Is this why animal fat tastes so sweet?

Nature is actually more basic than acidic - the ocean is basic and so are most plant and animal cells. Humans eat mostly acidic plants because we're taste-sensitive to alkaloids, many of which are poisonous. Meat is basic when living (pH ~7.2), but muscles produce lactic acid in breaking down glycogen after death, so it is somewhat acidic by the time we eat it.

The Wheelgun

This isn't a comprehensive dissertation by any means, just food for thought if you're in the market for a first, or moderately priced, defense weapon.

I think the venerable wheelgun is now one of the most overlooked defense weapons on the planet. When the time comes, and you're looking for that-one-gun, don't forget the wheely. I see a lot of young people and new shooters that ask things like "what should I get for my first?", "what's the best defense gun?", "shotgun or AR at home?", etc. Before you run out and buy a sub-compact polymer SA (in .45 'cause it's cool then you limp-wrist the shit out of it and complain that it's a piece of crap and won't feed any ammo,) an AR (that you'll mod to fucking death and be unable to hold up) or a tactical shorty scatter gun (in 12ga, of course, with a pistol grip - sure to break your wrist because you had no idea a slug or 00 hit so damn hard and would make you piss your pants,) stop. Stop and go put your hands on a revolver.

My personal favorite and [IMO] best: .357 Magnum. I have a very moderately priced Taurus hammered .357 mag with a 2" ported barrel. This is a fantastic weapon and the only one out of the safe at all times. This little gem sits nice and neat and tucked away on the bedside table and is always ready for action. I have some others, but this little thing is a beast. And don't think it won't bust someones ass.

Before I go in to why, understand that I have a couple safe's full of weapons. Weapons of all types, shapes and sizes. Most are purpose bought or built and all have a place. AR's and shotguns both serve well as defensive weapons, but not in the typical home [invasion] defense or concealed carry way. I think of them more as a defensive stand weapon. My polymers and 1911's are beautiful, powerful and awesome but, again, not my go-to for bedside. With everything I have, the revolver is still my defense weapon of choice.

There are too many reasons to really cover them all but here's my short list:

  • No-Thought Use - just pick it up and squeeze the trigger. This is, to me, the most salient point to having a revolver; no slide to rack, no failure to feed or eject, few moving parts, etc. This is the alligator of the gun world. All the other dinosaurs are extinct but this one keeps on going and is still just as kick ass as it always was. And, even better, limp wristing won't cause a fail to cycle - you might miss your target but the next round is ready to go no matter what.
  • .357 is a proven and powerfull caliber
  • A compact or subcompact revolver can be picked up for a very good price
  • If you get a .357 mag you can shoot .38's in the same gun - cheap practice/plinking
  • There are revolvers in many, many calibers - you can find one that suits you
  • Still Bad Ass - don't think so? Then you haven't seen a Dirty Harry .44 or a S&W 500. I don't exactly recommend them for CC, but they are tough as hell. *A little harder to conceal than the thinner sub / single stackers but still doable in the smaller models

Just a couple thoughts to help you on your journey to your first gun or a really great home defense gun. No, you won't get any with a 12+ round capacity but with some practice and a speed loader you can still get lots of rounds off quickly if you need to.

When you get ready to go try out a couple guns, don't forget to try a nice little wheel too.

Mine is a 5-shot Chief's Special. I load it with .38+P hollowpoints (so what if continued shooting will loosen it up? I don't care. It's for 1-5 shots in self-defense). I totally agree about the revolvers. Old, reliable (if clean), and if there's a misfire, pull the trigger again.
